title: Triangulated derived scalar extension computed on resolutions
statement: Let R and B be commutative rings with B an R-algebra [def-weil-module-base-change], module carriers in a universe containing both rings, and chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with a common morphism universe. Assume ordinary extension is additive. There exist a functor L:D(R) to D(B) and a counit Qh_R followed by L to ordinary homotopy scalar extension followed by Qh_B, exhibiting L as the total left derived functor. L has a shift structure for which it is triangulated. For every complex E there are a complex P and a quasi-isomorphism s:P to E such that the counit at P is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Resolve R-complexes by K-flat complexes [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], or the ordinary module functorial flat resolution construction. With unequal ring universes first lift the rings to the common module carrier universe and use the restriction equivalences along the lift ring isomorphisms. These equivalences preserve complexes, homotopies and quasi-isomorphisms.

Specialize fixed-second-factor tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] to B in degree zero and identify its ordinary total complex naturally with termwise extension of scalars. Thus quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat models are inverted after derived localization. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to obtain L, the universal counit, a shift structure and triangulatedness. Its counit is invertible on K-flat models. Transport this pair through the lift-ring equivalences when necessary. For each E retain a resolution P to E; the last clause is exactly counit invertibility at P.
